trigger: Month-end client reporting and engagement letter drafting overwhelming the team

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Donnie Azoff, Jordan Belfort from Eleno. I've heard Marlowe & Finch Accounting is the calmest thirty-four-person practice in Hawthorn, so tell me, who is actually carrying month-end in there?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: I'm Donnie, the CFO, and month-end is not calm at all. Client reporting and engagement letters are eating the team alive.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Then you're exactly who I built this pitch for. Picture it: three practices on your street have already signed, and the pilot price is gone Friday. It's $9,500 for the discovery phase and we start the build Monday. You don't need a committee, Donnie, you need engineers on the tools before another month-end swallows the place.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Hold on. I'm taking the call because we need options, not because we've chosen anyone. What are you actually proposing to build?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Two agents, fixed scope, no science project. One drafts the month-end client reporting pack straight out of your ledger, the other drafts engagement letters from your own templates. Both run inside your systems, the IP is yours, no subscription. And I can guarantee the agents never hallucinate, so nothing goes out with an invented number in it.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: That is a very big promise. We have thirty-four people and every one has an opinion about how a report reads.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Opinions are fine, we encode the loudest one. The discovery phase is two weeks: we sit with your reporting lead, map the templates and wire the ledger. The build runs six weeks after that. Managed optimisation afterwards is optional, not a leash.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Price is my first concern. The partners have just signed off a software budget and they will ask me what this replaces.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: It replaces the Sunday nights, Donnie. You'll halve your back-office headcount by Christmas, so the line item pays for itself twice over before the first lodgement of the new year. Price is smoke. Capacity is the fire.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: I am not cutting half my back office. Two of those people are the reason the reports come out right.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Fair enough, call it capacity released rather than seats removed. The point stands either way: your people stop moving figures out of one system and into another by hand, and start reviewing work that arrives already drafted.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: That part I like. Reviewing a draft beats building one from scratch. But there is a governance question sitting underneath all of this.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Governance is where we are strongest. None of our clients has ever had a compliance finding, and we run every engagement the same way: evidence at each step, review gates before anything sends, and a named engineer on the account.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Even so, the partners will want to know who signs off when the agent gets something wrong. Our current provider is slow, but nobody has ever had to answer that question about them.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: You sign off, exactly as you do today, except the draft arrives finished. And while we are here: Your incumbent is about to lose their ISO certification, which is its own answer to your governance question.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: About to lose certification? That is a serious thing to say out loud, and I have not heard it from anyone else.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Let's not get bogged down in that. The market is moving, and you do not want Marlowe & Finch Accounting to be the practice everyone talks about in the Hawthorn coffee queue.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: I do not like being rushed. What happens today if I say yes to reviewing something?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Today is easy. I turn this call into a plain proposal: the two agents, the scope of each, the discovery phase, the build weeks, who does what, and precisely what you own at the end of it.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: A clean pack is useful. I still need the managing partner comfortable before anyone signs anything here.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Of course. Give the managing partner the short version: two agents, fixed scope, running in your systems, the IP transferred to you, no ongoing subscription, and a number that does not move once it is signed.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Short and clear will help. He reads the first page and the last page, nothing else.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Then the first page carries the number and the last page carries the start date. I will get a proposal in your inbox today, with the statement of work attached so your managing partner can see the scope.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: I said review it, not sign it. If the scope is genuinely fixed, I can take it to him tonight.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: That is the small step, and the small step is all I am asking for. I will send the proposal and statement of work by 5pm today.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Fine. Send it by 5pm today, 11 September. I will review it with the managing partner, and if the scope matches what you have described, we will sign and start the discovery phase.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Excellent. I will send it to donnie@marlowefinch.example, and the first page will be painfully clear: $48,600 for the fixed-scope build, the discovery phase costed inside it, and the IP transferred to Marlowe & Finch Accounting at handover.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Copy nobody else for now. And Jordan, take the theatre out of the email. The partners like numbers, not fireworks.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Numbers only. The fireworks go in a separate attachment that mysteriously never arrives. Thanks Donnie, you have moved faster than anyone else on your street.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Right. Send the proposal. Goodbye.
